items.mathematical_rationale: The only mathematically valid reading here is the ideal generated by p-th powers of local sections of J, often denoted J^[p], not the ordinary product power. On an affine open, base change by Frobenius sends A/J to A/(a^p:a∈J). For A=F_2[x,y], J=(x,y), the generated ideal is (x^2,y^2), whereas the ordinary square also contains xy. The Nakayama argument remains valid: for a proper ideal in a local ring, J^[p]⊂mJ; J=J^[p] with J finitely generated forces J=0. This resolves the meaning, without claiming the original author explicitly defined a special notation.

items.mathematical_rationale: The auxiliary claim is false for arbitrary R because tensoring the short exact sequence need not preserve left exactness. Counterexample: A=Z/4, I=(2), A_0=F_2, S_0=(0→0→F_2→F_2→0), R=F_2. Any projective lift Q of Q_0=F_2 is Z/4; its surjection to R has kernel F_2, whose reduction is nonzero, contradicting P_0=0. Adding R flat makes Tor_1^A(A_0,R)=0 and repairs exactness. In the actual descending construction R_0=Z_0^{i+1} is projective, so choose a projective (hence flat) lift R by Lemma3(ii); thus the corollary and subsequent lemma proofs remain valid.
